intro.speakerLine: You stand in the great hall of Camelot while Saxon warbands gather beyond the border. Speak plainly—what brings you before the Round Table?
intro.context: 5th–6th century legendary Britain, uniting fractured kingdoms against Saxon raids.

choices.label: Offer counsel on uniting the rival British lords
Ask whether the Round Table truly makes every knight equal

council.speakerLine: A wise answer. Swords alone cannot hold Britain if our own kings quarrel over old grudges while the borders burn.
council.context: Arthurian tradition centers on forging alliances among fractious regional rulers.

choices.label: Pledge your support and take your leave

round_table.speakerLine: No seat sits higher than another here. When every lord shares the same table, pride gives way to shared duty.
round_table.context: First described by Wace in 1155, the Round Table symbolized chivalric equality.

choices.label: Pledge your support and take your leave

ending.speakerLine: Camelot remembers those who stand with it in uncertain hours. Go in peace, friend.
